summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal (a Python LangChain single-agent with memory and three tools) and, together with the supplied run-environment skill.md and the installed documentdb-* skills, provides enough to start a build. Several implementation details are unspecified (Python version, LLM/embedding choices, exact orders schema, seed-data source, indexing choices, run/test commands), so the builder will make sensible defaults described below.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LangChain agent with agent memory that connects to DocumentDB and has tools for fetching order history, running aggregation pipelines for spend summaries, and looking up individual order status"
rubric.note: Clear user/problem and what sample should demonstrate (conversation-aware order history & spend summaries).

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Python LangChain agent" (single agent with tools / agent memory)

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Target a modern Python 3.10+ runtime (virtualenv), e.g., support CPython 3.10 or 3.11. Use pip for dependency installation.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill.md mention Python and pip but do not fix a minor version; builder will pick a recent 3.x version.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use pymongo (the official Python MongoDB driver), e.g., pymongo >= 4.3 compatible with MongoDB 7.x; create a singleton MongoClient reused across requests.
rubric.note: Installed documentdb-driver skill gives driver best-practices (singleton MongoClient, connection reuse).

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) ... connection string in environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI ... Use the database named sample_retail_06"
rubric.note: The supplied run-environment skill.md gives explicit cluster/tier and database to use; the build must target this existing cluster.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file... use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder"
rubric.note: Where to read the connection string and that it must not be committed is explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "fetching order history ... lookup individual order status" (implies an orders collection)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create an orders collection with a simple, conventional retail schema: order_id (string, unique), customer_id, order_date (ISODate), items[] (sku, qty, price), total_amount (number), status (string). No sharding by default (single-shard cluster), no >16MB docs.
rubric.note: The prompt implies an orders collection but does not specify exact fields, types, or shard key; documentdb-data-modeling can guide choices but not the exact schema.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a small synthetic seed script (seed.py) that inserts a few hundred orders across several customers. The seed script should be idempotent (upsert by order_id) so it can be re-run.
rubric.note: No source, size, or load method specified; skill.md asks to "load the sample data" during verification but doesn't supply it.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "tools for fetching order history, running aggregation pipelines for spend summaries, and looking up individual order status"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement find() for customer order history (filter by customer_id, sort by order_date desc, limit/paginate). Implement aggregation pipelines for spend summaries (total_spent, order_count) including a 'last month' pipeline. Create indexes: single-field index on customer_id, compound (customer_id + order_date) or separate order_date index, and unique index on order_id.
rubric.note: The prompt requires find() and aggregation pipelines but does not specify index shapes; installed indexing skill can guide index choices.

rubric.found_in_prompt: mentions LangChain agent but no LLM/embedding provider or models
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Default to OpenAI for models: Chat model via environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY (e.g., gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o), and embeddings via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims). Provide env var placeholders in .env.example for provider keys.
rubric.note: Model/embedding provider, exact models and dims are not specified and will materially affect vector index choices if used.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a simple CLI interactive script (run_agent.py) demonstrating conversation turns and a small programmatic example/test that shows sequence: ask history -> follow-up 'what about last month?'. Optionally include a minimal HTTP API wrapper, but primary surface is CLI/test.
rubric.note: Prompt does not mandate CLI vs API or web UI; builder will pick an interactive CLI + automated test to demonstrate behavior.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... Do not read or change other databases on the cluster."
rubric.note: The environment explicitly says use the existing cluster; do not provision new resources.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: README will include: pip install -r requirements.txt; copy .env.example -> .env and fill DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY; python seed.py; python run_agent.py; pytest to run unit tests. The builder will add concrete commands for the chosen Python version and virtualenv activation.
rubric.note: No concrete commands or expected outputs are present in the prompt or skills.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Acceptance criteria: agent runs, tools are registered, memory persists last-customer and last-time-range across turns, aggregation and find tools run against sample_retail_06.orders, and the example/test demonstrates resolving 'what about last month?' to the correct customer/time-range results.
rubric.note: Not explicitly stated; builder will create pragmatic acceptance checks.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision new cloud resources; keep secrets out of repo; keep sample lightweight and free-tier friendly where possible. No production HA or CMK work is required.
rubric.note: Prompt does not call out cost or scope constraints except via skill.md guidance not to create resources.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: "use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Repository will include: README.md, requirements.txt (pinned), .env.example with placeholders (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY), src/ or agent/ layout, seed.py, run_agent.py, tests/, .gitignore. Use the name 'Azure DocumentDB' in docs.
rubric.note: Some conventions are implied by skill.md (.env.example), but many conventions (pin deps, tests) are not explicitly specified.

contradictions: The prompt says "Using the DocumentDB skill" but there is no single installed skill named exactly "DocumentDB"; instead multiple documentdb-* skills are available (documentdb-driver, documentdb-connection, documentdb-data-modeling, etc.). Builder will combine these skills, but the wording could be interpreted as a missing single-skill name.
questions_for_author: Which LLM and embedding provider/models should the sample use by default (OpenAI, Anthropic, local model)? This affects embeddings dims and code examples.
Which exact Python minor version should we target (e.g., 3.10 or 3.11)?
Should unit tests be runnable without a live cluster (i.e., use mocks) or is verifying against the live cluster acceptable for CI/local testing?
requirements_at_risk: fetch_order_history tool must include pagination/limit logic — prompt implies fetch but does not specify pagination; builder will likely implement a page/limit but this requirement is not explicit.

seed script that loads sample data and creates the index and can be run twice without duplicating data — prompt/skill.md asks to load sample data but does not require idempotent seeding; installed skills don't provide a repo seed script.

Executable example or unit test that demonstrates conversational context resolution — prompt requests correct resolution of 'what about last month?' but does not explicitly require an automated example/test; risk the builder provides only a manual demo.
Handling empty results and DB errors gracefully — prompt doesn't explicitly require friendly error handling; risk of minimal error messages if builder omits explicit handling.

Vector index dimensions must match embedding model output and index parameters chosen for sample size — prompt mentions cluster is vector-capable in skill.md but does not choose embedding model or index dims; this mapping is not specified.
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — skill.md suggests using a .env.example but does not enumerate all env vars required by the agent (LLM keys, other options).
Search results include similarity score (if vector search used) — prompt doesn't mention vector search result formatting; skill.md notes vector-capable cluster but not how to surface scores.
Dependencies pinned in requirements.txt — neither prompt nor skills require pinned dependencies; builder may or may not pin versions.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — prompt/skill.md expect verification against live cluster but do not require tests to mock the DB for offline execution.
Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster — prompt/skill.md explicitly say a cluster already exists and not to provision another; the gallery requirement to provide infra code is not covered.
